## New Cross-Domain Connection

- **[2026-10-31] Lightfin knows who framed him only because a magic comb showed him. Off Duty, the wrongful-conviction series Fred just finished, shows why that would not be enough to clear him: once the police are a party to the case, only evidence they cannot wave away overturns it.** [[lightfin/story-arc-lightfin]] ends Mermaid's Comb with Lightfin certain that Chief Raggy Tooth and the Megaladon framed him, but every proof he holds is Veta's vision. The physical frame is still intact: the coins planted in his desk drawer, the firing, and the ONN broadcast. [[podcasts/podcast-off-duty-the-guardian-episodes-1-8]] follows a 12-year fight to undo a verdict in a case where the victim was a police officer. It takes the evidence apart link by link (interrogation statements, police conduct, digital forensics, the prosecution's choices) and ends on whether the system will correct itself at all. That is Lightfin's situation exactly: the institution that has to clear him is run by the man who framed him. The 10-10 Austin Tice connection gives the arc a way to find the truth (retrace the route; an overlooked figure carries the reveal). Off Duty adds the step after that: proving it. Concrete test for the unfiled finale outlines: does the ending replace the comb vision with one piece of physical evidence that Shark PD cannot ignore? Two candidates: who had access to Lightfin's desk drawer, and the treasure found in the sunken trawler with Raggy Tooth present. And who outside Shark PD (Ray Manta re-broadcasting on ONN, or Dwight finally backing him up) forces the reversal in public? Caveat: the Off Duty page's episode topics come from titles and the series synopsis only.

## New investigation idea

- **[2026-10-30] The paper book's "−15% stop" has never filled at −15%. All seven pure stop-outs filled worse, at an average of about −17.6%, and the page that tracks them says no slippage is modelled.** [[finance/paper-trading/paper-trading-performance]] lists QCOM −17.3%, AIP −19.6%, SKYT −18.4%, PENG −15.9%, LRCX −18.2%, FICO −15.9% and, on 10-29, FTNT −18.1% (it gapped through $144.36 on its Q3 print). Its own assumptions section still says "No slippage, commission, or spread modelled". The live book had the same failure in the same week: [[finance/trading-portfolio]]'s SFM fell 22.6% after Q3, straight through its $60.85 stop. So the real loss per stopped trade is about 17% bigger than the rules assume. That feeds directly into the 10-28 sizing gap (the Kelly and ruin pages would use −15% as the loss leg). Next steps: (1) add a "realised stop loss" line (mean and worst) to the performance page's assumptions; (2) use the Phase 17 earnings calendar to flag any open position with a report inside 5 trading days. The next test is MCK, whose own thesis names its 2026-11-04 report as the key risk; (3) let strategy-feedback decide whether to trim, widen the stop, or simply accept the gap risk before a print.
